title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling Playbook & Benchmarking Suite
author: Emily Chen
content:
Summary

This page consolidates canonical documentation for the Redwood Serving Runtime: architecture overview, kernel scheduling model, profiling & benchmarking playbooks, release notes highlights, known issues, and operational runbooks. It is the single-source reference for runtime engineers, SRE, and performance-oriented reviewers.

Goals
- Describe runtime components and responsibilities.
- Provide reproducible profiling and benchmarking steps.
- Document kernel scheduling heuristics and tuning knobs.
- Provide operational runbooks and known-issues with mitigations.

Runtime architecture (high level)

Overview:
- Service name: redwood-serving-runtime (runtimesrv).
- Primary components: Frontend API (frontend-svc), Router/Dispatcher (dispatcher-svc), Batch Scheduler (batch-svc), Executor (executor-svc), KV Cache (kvcache-svc), Model Loader (modelmgr-svc), Metrics/Tracing (prometheus, jaeger).
- Deployment model: multi-tenant host process per GPU node, isolated worker processes for protected tenants (Dedicated/Private).

Component responsibilities:
1. frontend-svc: HTTP/gRPC entrypoint, request validation, auth (KMS token checks).
2. dispatcher-svc: request routing, policy enforcement (latency-first/cost-first/region), prefix cache lookup.
3. batch-svc: continuous batching engine, maintains per-model queues, assembles micro-batches to match kernel optimal shapes.
4. executor-svc: invokes optimized kernels, manages KV cache, performs token generation loop.
5. modelmgr-svc: model artifacts, quantization profiles, fallback variants.
6. kvcache-svc: off-heap prefix storage, LRU sharding per worker.

SLOs and operational thresholds
- 95th percentile response latency (small-chat workload, 128 tokens): <= 120 ms.
- p99 latency: <= 300 ms (hosted tier).
- Token throughput per GPU (A100-80GB): baseline 20k tokens/sec for OPT-30B fp16 with batching policy smart-128.
- Error budget: 99.9% success rate per 24h window.

Kernel scheduling model

Design principles:
- Optimize for latency-sensitive single-shot requests and high-throughput batched workloads.
- Maintain determinism for KV cache lifetime and sequence alignment.

Key concepts:
- Micro-batches: small variable-length groups (1-32) used to amortize kernel launch overhead.
- Kernel selection table: matches (model-arch, seq-length, dtype, hardware) to kernel version and tiling parameters.
- Preemptible epochs: short windows where higher-priority requests can preempt long-running batches.
- Backpressure signals: queue_depth, avg_wait_ms, gpu_util.

Tunable knobs (config file: /etc/redwood/batcher.conf):
| parameter | description | default | range |
| max_microbatch_size | Upper bound for micro-batch aggregation | "32" | 1-128 |
| latency_target_ms | Soft SLO for per-batch assembly | "20" | 1-200 |
| preempt_fraction | Fraction of slots reserved for high-priority | "0.15" | 0.0-0.5 |
| kv_cache_eviction_ms | idle eviction window for KV cache entries | "600000" | ms |

Examples:
- To prioritize latency for chat endpoints set preempt_fraction=0.25 and latency_target_ms=10.
- For high throughput offline workloads set max_microbatch_size=64 and latency_target_ms=50.

Profiling playbook (step-by-step)

Prerequisites:
- Access to perf nodes (tag: perf) and Prometheus/Jaeger.
- Binary builds with symbols: docker image redwood/runtimesrv:perf-<gitsha>.
- Profiling tools installed on node: nvprof/nsys, perf, python3, py-spy.

Quick profiling checklist:
1. Reproduce workload: use benchmark client at tools/perf/bench_client.py with same prompt distribution.
2. Capture end-to-end traces: enable jaeger sampling at 1.0 for short run: curl -X POST ... (see infra snippet).
3. Kernel-level trace: run nsys capture around executor-svc process: 
   nsys profile -o run1 --capture-range=kernel --sample=cpu --trace=cuda -- python3 run_client.py --duration 120
4. GPU metrics: collect GPU SM utilization, memory BW via nvidia-smi dmon and DCGM.
5. Flamegraphs: generate CPU flamegraphs with py-spy: py-spy record -o flame.svg -- python3 executor_main.py --run-profile
6. Token-level timing: enable token_timing flag on executor and export to /tmp/token_timings.json

Interpretation guidance:
- If avg_kernel_launch_ms > 1.2x expected: investigate kernel choice (use kernel selection debug: /debug/kernel-table).
- If many small kernels dominate: increase max_microbatch_size or enable fused attention kernels.
- High memory copies: check pinned-memory / use zero-copy paths.

Benchmarking suite

Repository & runner:
- tools/perf/ contains benchmark manifests and runner: bench_runner.py.
- Manifests are YAML files under perf/manifests/ describing model, sequence length distribution, client QPS, concurrency, and warmup.

Standard benchmark profiles (stored in perf/manifests):
- chat-small: 95% short (<64 tokens) chat messages.
- chat-long: 20% long (>512 tokens) tails.
- embed-bulk: embedding-only throughput tests.

Reproducible run example:
1. Start driver: ./bench_runner.py --manifest perf/manifests/chat-small.yaml --duration 180 --targets node:perf-01
2. Collect metrics: prometheus scrape, nsys capture, bench result JSON saved to /tmp/bench-chat-small-<ts>.json
3. Post-process: python3 tools/perf/aggregate_results.py --input /tmp/bench-*.json --output results/report-<ts>.html

Reporting and thresholds:
- Bench results include avg latency, p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, power draw.
- Report must include hardware spec and docker image gitsha.
- Passing criteria for a release: for relevant profiles, p95 latency regression <= 5% and throughput regression <= 7% vs baseline.

Release notes (recent highlights)
- 2027-11-15 (v3.2.0): Introduced preemptible epochs and improved kernel selection table for fused attention kernels (+18% throughput on OPT workloads).
- 2027-12-10 (v3.2.1): Fix: memory leak in kvcache on long-running sessions (kv_cache_eviction_ms defaults changed).
- 2028-01-12 (v3.3.0): New perf image with nsys-compatible symbols and improved micro-batching for long-tail sequences.

Known issues and mitigations

1) Symptom: Occasional p99 spikes during bursty traffic.
- Cause: long-running batches delaying preemptible slots.
- Mitigation: increase preempt_fraction or enable adaptive_preempt=true (flag in dispatcher).

2) Symptom: OOM in executor when serving multiple large-models concurrently.
- Cause: simultaneous KV cache growth and model weights loaded in MPS.
- Mitigation: set model_oom_policy=unload_least_recent and limit_per_node_models=3.

3) Symptom: Stale KV cache after rollback to older model variant.
- Cause: cache key format changed in 2027-10-01.
- Mitigation: run kvcache flush tool: ./tools/kvcache/flush --model <model-id> --confirm

Runbooks (operational playbooks)

A. High tail latency (p99 > target)
1. Confirm: check dashboards: dashboards/runtimes/latency-overview (last 60m).
2. Identify impacted nodes: filter node:perf or cluster:prod and check queue_depth > 50.
3. Actions:
   - Increase preempt_fraction to 0.25 via /api/admin/configs and roll out to dispatchers.
   - If root cause is model-specific, activate fallback to compatible variant (api: /api/models/<id>/fallback).
   - If sustained, scale GPU pool by +2 nodes (autoscaler override).
4. Post-incident: run bench_runner profile for 30m and attach results.

B. Executor OOMs
1. Restart executor on affected node with stale model unloading: systemctl restart executor-svc --no-block
2. Run ./tools/diag/memory_snapshot.sh and upload to s3://redwood-diagnostics/<incident-id>/
3. If repeated, reduce concurrency_limit on node: echo 2 > /sys/fs/redwood/concurrency_limit

C. Model load failures on startup
1. Inspect modelmgr logs: journalctl -u modelmgr-svc -n 200.
2. Verify artifact integrity: sha256sum /models/<model>.tar.gz and compare to catalog.
3. Fallback: load quantized variant using: /api/models/<id>/load?variant=quantized

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Run a targeted benchmark:
  docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work -w /work redwood/perf:latest python3 bench_runner.py --manifest perf/manifests/chat-small.yaml --duration 180
- Enable debug kernel table (temporary): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://dispatcher.internal/debug/kernel-table?enable=true
- Flush KV cache for a node: ssh node-01 sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kvcache-flush --all

If you find contradictory or out-of-date items on this page, file a docs PR against confluence/eng-serving-runtime and add @perf-team as reviewer.
